newsitem.title: USA: Branson taking donations to cover tourism tax.
newsitem.headline: Branson taking donations to cover tourism tax.

text.p: Branson has started a donation program to recoup funds lost when the Missouri Supreme Court overturned a tourism tax that backed $46 million of bonds, a city spokesman said Thursday.
Debt service on the bonds sold to build drinking and wastewater treatment plans has been covered by a reserve fund created when the tax challenge lawsuit was filed, spokesman Jerry Adams said.
Money received through the donation program announced Monday will be used to pay off principal amounts, Adams said.

Businesses participating have opted to make voluntary collections of the surcharge or include it in the cost of tickets or lodging and remit the money to a Springfield, Missouri, accounting firm, Adams said.
The firm will hold all donations confidential and distribute 75 percent of the money to the city and 25 percent to the chamber of commerce as the tourism tax had been divided, Adams said.
The 4 percent tourism tax had generated about $500,000 per month in July and August historically and the city has no estimate how much it will receive in donations, Adams said.
Missouri Gov. Mel Carnahan has said that lawmakers likely will address the Supreme Court decision in a special session in September.

The Supreme Court had found the law "facially special" and noted that it applied only to a municipality with 3,000 to 5,000 residents, more than 5,000 hotel and motel rooms within city limits and located in a county bordering on Arkansas.
